title: Bound on half-threshold influential coordinates
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a Boolean function. Let $t$ be a positive rational and let $\\varepsilon$ be a rational with $0<\\varepsilon\\leq\\frac12$. For each coordinate $i$, let its influence be the uniform probability that flipping $i$ changes $f$, and let the total influence be the sum of the squared discrete derivatives of the associated real-valued function. If this total influence is at most $t$, then the number of coordinates whose influence is at least half of $\\theta=\\frac12(\\varepsilon/8)^2t^{-2}(1/9)^{\\lceil t/ (\\varepsilon/8)\\rceil}$ is at most $\\left\\lceil 2t/\\theta\\right\\rceil$.
hypotheses_covered: The total influence of the real-valued version of $f$ is at most $t$
